# Native containers and public accessors

SpaMTP keeps raw, unaligned spectra in Cardinal and feature-by-pixel matrices
in `SpatialExperiment`. Public accessors read, modify and subset these
containers. This guide uses real mouse-brain mass spectrometry imaging (MSI)
and paired RNA to demonstrate the native API; historical Seurat tutorials use
different interfaces.

## Migrating existing scripts {#migrating-existing-scripts}

The native API uses lower-camel-case names and Bioconductor containers. These
common calls replace their historical Seurat-oriented counterparts:

| Historical call | Current interface | Input or behaviour to review |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `NormalizeSMData()` | `normalizeSMData()` | Select the native modality with `assay` and input layer with `slot` |
| `RunMetabolicPCA()` | `runMetabolicPCA()` | Scores are stored in `reducedDim()` |
| `FindAllDEMs()` | `findAllDEMs()` | Choose descriptive markers or a biological-replicate model explicitly |
| `AnnotateSM()` | `annotateSM()` | Indexed, scored candidates are stored with reference provenance |
| `FindRegionalPathways()` | `findRegionalPathways()` | Supply reconciled identities and complete regional rankings |
| `MultiOmicIntegration()` | `multiOmicIntegration()` | Concatenates scaled PCA embeddings with equal modality weights |
| Seurat `GetAssayData()` | `SummarizedExperiment::assay()` | Read a named matrix from the main or `altExp()` experiment |

Convert a historical object with `seuratToSpatialExperiment()` before these
calls, then check feature IDs, paired location names and matrix scales. Recompute
reductions and pathway results using the selected native layers; equal-weight
embedding concatenation defines the current integration method.

## Public accessors

| Data to access | Public interface |
|---|---|
| Expression/intensity matrices | `assay()`, `assayNames()` |
| Feature m/z and annotations | `rowData()` |
| Pixel metadata and groups | `colData()`, `colLabels()` |
| Pixel coordinates | `spatialCoords()`, `spatialCoordsNames()` |
| Optical images | `imgData()`, `imgRaster()`, `addImg()` |
| Paired modalities | `altExp()`, `altExpNames()` |
| PCA and other embeddings | `reducedDim()`, `reducedDimNames()` |
| Analysis provenance | `metadata()` |

Replacement forms modify data, for example `colData(spe)$region <- values`.

## Modality and expression layer

`assay = "SPT"` selects `altExp(spe, "SPT")` in this example;
`slot = "counts"` selects its raw-count matrix. Use `assay = "main"` for
the primary experiment. These selectors require exact names. See
`help("experimentAccess", package = "SpaMTP")` for aliases.

```{r load-package, message=FALSE}
library(SpaMTP)
```

# Mouse-brain MSI and paired RNA

SpaMTPData supplies the complete archived mouse-brain striatal dataset: MSI
and paired Visium RNA with anatomical regions, lesion-side labels and image
coordinates. Its spatial coverage follows the source archive's MSI-cluster
selection from the striatal section. The [complete workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html)
uses the same data for regional analysis. The first load downloads the pinned
resource unless a verified local or cached copy is available.

```{r brain-data}
spe <- SpaMTPData::spaMTPData("mouse_brain_dhb_striatum", version = "1.1.0")
rna <- SingleCellExperiment::altExp(spe, "SPT")
data.frame(
  modality = c("MSI", "RNA"),
  features = c(nrow(spe), nrow(rna)),
  paired_locations = c(ncol(spe), ncol(rna)))
```

`RegionLoupe` includes ACB (nucleus accumbens), CP (caudoputamen), OT
(olfactory tubercle) and aco (anterior commissure, olfactory limb). `lesion`
retains the source side labels. Regional and side differences describe spatial
variation within this single specimen. Biological replication requires
independent specimens.

# Read a binned MSI table

`readSMMatrix()` expects one row per pixel, coordinates named `x`/`y` and
numeric m/z column names. This round trip writes eight measured masses at
**every supplied location** to a temporary CSV. It demonstrates the file
format; subsequent analysis uses the complete `spe` object above.

`project.name` sets the imported sample label. The CSV importer generates
pixel IDs from coordinates, so archived barcodes and RNA pairing must be
retained separately. For raw imzML input, see the
[native workflow](SpaMTP_Bioconductor.html).

```{r read-matrix}
intensity <- SummarizedExperiment::assay(spe, "counts")
mz <- SummarizedExperiment::rowData(spe)$mz
xy <- SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(spe)
export_features <- unique(round(seq(1, nrow(spe), length.out = 8)))
input <- data.frame(xy, t(as.matrix(intensity[export_features, ])),
  check.names = FALSE)
names(input) <- c("x", "y", as.character(mz[export_features]))

imported <- local({
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
  on.exit(unlink(path))
  utils::write.csv(input, path, row.names = FALSE)
  readSMMatrix(path, project.name = "mouse_brain", verbose = FALSE)
})
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
  as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(imported, "counts")),
  as.matrix(intensity[export_features, ]), check.attributes = FALSE)))
SummarizedExperiment::rowData(imported)$mz
```

# Pixel and feature metadata

Rows identify measured MSI features; columns identify paired locations.
`colLabels()` sets the default grouping to the archived anatomy without
changing `RegionLoupe`. The first table shows each region's coverage on both
sides; the second summarizes per-location quality control (QC) measurements.

```{r metadata-access}
SingleCellExperiment::colLabels(spe) <- factor(spe$RegionLoupe)
SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe)$total_intensity <- Matrix::colSums(intensity)
SummarizedExperiment::colData(spe)$detected_features <- Matrix::colSums(intensity > 0)
table(region = spe$RegionLoupe, side = spe$lesion)
qc <- list(total_intensity = spe$total_intensity,
    detected_features = spe$detected_features)
qc_summary <- data.frame(
    metric = names(qc),
    minimum = vapply(qc, min, numeric(1)),
    median = vapply(qc, stats::median, numeric(1)),
    maximum = vapply(qc, max, numeric(1)))
knitr::kable(qc_summary, digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
```

`total_intensity` sums the measured MSI intensities at each location;
`detected_features` counts MSI features with intensity above zero.
The feature-level accessor `rowData(spe)$mz` stores one measured m/z per row.

## Normalized expression

`normalizeSMData(..., "LogNormalize")` adds `logcounts` while retaining raw
`counts`. For locations with positive total intensity, the default transformation is
`log1p(10000 * intensity / total_intensity)`, using the supplied MSI features
and natural logarithms.
`metadata(spe)$spamtp_normalization` records the method, source assay and scale
factor.

Figure 2.\@ref(fig:expression-access) displays the mass nearest m/z 400.14659,
a focal feature in the original mouse-brain tutorial. `feature` is its row ID; the title reports
the actual measured m/z. Metabolite identification requires additional
chemical evidence.

```{r expression-access, fig.width=7, fig.height=4.5, out.width="760px", fig.cap="A measured mouse-brain mass feature across archived anatomical regions. Each point is one paired location; colour marks the archived lesion side. Boxes pool both sides within each region and show the median and interquartile range; whiskers extend to 1.5 times that range. The displayed mass is the measured feature nearest m/z 400.14659 from the original mouse-brain tutorial. The plot describes within-specimen distributions, which depend on regional composition and spatial relationships."}
spe <- normalizeSMData(spe, "LogNormalize", verbose = FALSE)
feature_index <- which.min(abs(mz - 400.14659))
feature <- rownames(spe)[feature_index]
scater::plotExpression(spe, features = feature, x = "RegionLoupe",
  colour_by = "lesion", exprs_values = "logcounts",
  show_violin = FALSE, show_boxplot = TRUE, point_size = 0.8) +
  ggplot2::labs(x = "Archived anatomical region", colour = "Archived side",
    title = sprintf("Measured m/z %.4f", mz[feature_index]))
```

CP dominates this archived selection; sparse regions remain visible as
individual points. The region labels connect the expression profile to anatomy.
Regional composition should be examined before interpreting a side difference;
the [complete workflow](End_to_End_Workflow.html) illustrates regional marker
scoring and spatial sensitivity.

# Coordinates and optical images

## Coordinate axes and units

`spatialCoords()` retains the original image-pixel positions; y increases
downwards. Its rows follow the same locations as the assay columns. Inspect
axis names before combining data from another coordinate system.

```{r coordinate-access}
SpatialExperiment::spatialCoordsNames(spe)
stopifnot(identical(rownames(xy), colnames(spe)))
data.frame(axis = colnames(xy), minimum = apply(xy, 2, min),
  maximum = apply(xy, 2, max))
```

Coordinate names label the stored axes. Unit conversion, axis reversal and
image registration require explicit transformations. This example retains
the source coordinates.

## Image storage and registration

`imgData()` records each image's sample ID, image ID and scale factor. The
following artificial raster demonstrates image storage in a separate copy.
Histology registration requires a tissue image and a coordinate transform.
`load = TRUE` retains the raster after the temporary file is removed.

```{r image-access}
image_example <- local({
  path <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
  on.exit(unlink(path))
  png::writePNG(matrix(seq(0, 1, length.out = 12), nrow = 3), path)
  addSpatialImage(spe, imageSource = path, sampleId = unique(spe$sample_id),
    imageId = "storage-demo", scaleFactor = 1, load = TRUE)
})
SpatialExperiment::imgData(image_example)[, c("sample_id", "image_id", "scaleFactor")]
raster <- SpatialExperiment::imgRaster(image_example,
  sample_id = unique(spe$sample_id), image_id = "storage-demo")
stopifnot(inherits(raster, "raster"))
```

# Paired modalities and standard subsetting

`altExp(spe, "SPT")` contains the measured RNA at the same locations as MSI.
RNA and MSI features have independent row sets.

The existing pairing is checked before selecting the ACB locations. Column
subsetting keeps RNA and coordinates aligned; row subsetting affects only
the main MSI experiment.

```{r paired-access}
rna <- SingleCellExperiment::altExp(spe, "SPT")
stopifnot(identical(colnames(rna), colnames(spe)))
SingleCellExperiment::altExpNames(spe)
SummarizedExperiment::assayNames(rna)

accumbens <- spe[, spe$RegionLoupe == "ACB"]
accumbens_rna <- SingleCellExperiment::altExp(accumbens, "SPT")
data.frame(locations = ncol(accumbens), mass_features = nrow(accumbens),
  RNA_features = nrow(accumbens_rna))
stopifnot(identical(colnames(accumbens_rna), colnames(accumbens)),
  nrow(SpatialExperiment::spatialCoords(accumbens)) == ncol(accumbens))
```

For newly collected modalities, perform alignment and pairing first with
`mapSpatialOmics()`. `addTranscriptome()` checks and reorders an already paired
matrix by column names. These names must represent verified spatial matches.
Both modalities must contain the same set of unique location names.

## Analysis provenance

The resource identity, version and checksum remain in `metadata()`. Add
analysis settings alongside them so normalization and grouping are recoverable.

```{r provenance-access}
S4Vectors::metadata(spe)$analysis <- list(
  input_type = "paired mouse-brain MSI and Visium RNA",
  normalization = "LogNormalize", grouping = "RegionLoupe")
S4Vectors::metadata(spe)$SpaMTPData
```

The [annotation pipeline](Metabolite_Annotation_Pipeline.html) adds candidate
identities to `rowData()` and records annotation provenance in `metadata()`.

# Optional Seurat boundary

## Explicit conversion

Optional SeuratObject enables explicit conversion. SpaMTP uses Seurat 5 public
APIs: `LayerData()` for expression, double brackets for metadata, and
`GetTissueCoordinates()` for image/FOV coordinates. Update incompatible older
objects with `SeuratObject::UpdateSeuratObject()` in the Seurat workflow.

`seurat` is `spe` exported to Seurat; `values`, `pixel_metadata`,
`feature_metadata` and `centres` read its counts and metadata.
`converted` imports `counts` and `fov` coordinates.
`full = FALSE` returns one centroid per pixel; checks
verify pixel order and counts after the round trip.

```{r optional-conversion}
if (requireNamespace("SeuratObject", quietly = TRUE)) {
  seurat <- spatialExperimentToSeurat(spe)
  values <- SeuratObject::LayerData(seurat, assay = "Spatial", layer = "counts")
  pixel_metadata <- seurat[[]]
  feature_metadata <- seurat[["Spatial"]][[]]
  centres <- SeuratObject::GetTissueCoordinates(seurat, image = "fov", full = FALSE)

  converted <- seuratToSpatialExperiment(seurat, image = "fov", layer = "counts")
  stopifnot(identical(colnames(converted), colnames(spe)))
  stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(
    as.matrix(SummarizedExperiment::assay(converted, "counts")), as.matrix(values))))
  S4Vectors::metadata(converted)$seurat_interoperability
}
```

## Coordinate and layer selection

A single image/FOV supplies coordinates by default; metadata is used only
when no image exists. With multiple images, specify `image` or named
`coordinates`. Conversion represents each pixel by its centroid.

Only the named layer is transferred; join split Seurat layers first to include
the complete dataset. Unpaired assays are skipped with a warning. Optical
rasters, graphs and reductions are omitted. Continue with native accessors
after conversion.
